2	
3	## Scope
4	
5	Flutter/Dart project — "E2E" here means the project's own established
6	convention of `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` files: the real DI graph (`sl`),
7	real `Cubit` -> `Repository` -> `DataSource` -> `ApiClient` -> `Dio`
8	pipeline (both real interceptors attached), with only the transport
9	boundary (`HttpClientAdapter`) and native plugins faked (no
10	device/simulator/CI exists yet per AGENTS.md). Playwright/browser E2E
11	does not apply to this codebase.
12	
13	Target feature: **export** (story 7.1 — request a period export & job
14	status tracking), chosen because capture, entries, and chat already had
15	this level of coverage; export did not.
16	
17	## Generated Tests
18	
19	### E2E Tests
20	
21	- [x] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — 5 tests, driven
22	  directly against the real, DI-resolved `ExportJobCubit`:
23	  - Happy path: `start()` → genuine `export-summary-create` POST (URL,
24	    headers, periodEnd bumped to local end-of-day before UTC
25	    conversion) → real `Timer.periodic` poll loop → genuine
26	    `export-status-get/{jobId}` GETs → Pendente → Processando →
27	    Concluído (`ExportOutcome.narrativeReady`); also asserts polling
28	    really stops once terminal.
29	  - Narrativa falhou: `narrativeStatus: failed` maps to
30	    `ExportOutcome.narrativeUnavailable` through the real DTO mapping.
31	  - Período vazio: `errorCode: EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` maps through the
32	    real `Failure.fromCode` → `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`.
33	  - Erro: a non-empty-period error code (`AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`) maps
34	    to the generic `ExportJobState.error`.
35	  - Review-patch coverage: `export-summary-create` failing with a
36	    *retryable* code (`RATE_LIMITED`) is never retried — proves
37	    `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions`' real wiring for this
38	    function (previously only exercised in isolation or against a fake
39	    repository, never through the real Dio pipeline).
40	
41	- [x] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` / `test/features/export/
42	  export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — closed a test-pinning gap flagged by
43	  spec-7-2's round-2 code review (`deferred-work.md`): the mocked unit
44	  test now captures the `options` argument to `getRedirectLocation`'s
45	  `Dio.get` call and asserts `followRedirects == false` and the
46	  permissive `validateStatus` boundary (302 true / 400 false); the e2e
47	  test now asserts `followRedirects` on the request that actually
48	  reached the fake transport adapter, after passing through the real
49	  header + retry interceptor chain. Previously, flipping or dropping
50	  `followRedirects: false` in `ApiClient.getRedirectLocation` would not
51	  have failed either test.
52	
53	This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
54	`export_job_cubit_test.dart` (fake repository, I/O-matrix transitions),
55	`export_remote_data_source_test.dart` (mocked `ApiClient`, DTO
56	decoding), `export_status_sheet_test.dart` (widget rendering per
57	state), and `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s "export entry point"
58	group (tap → picker → `start()` → sheet, against a fake repository).
59	None of those drove a real network/poll round trip end to end.
60	
61	### API Tests
62	
63	Not applicable separately — the backend contract is exercised through
64	the same e2e suite above (real `ApiClient`/`Dio`/interceptors against a
65	faked transport), consistent with how every other feature in this
66	project is tested (no standalone HTTP-level test layer exists outside
67	this pattern).

# Test Automation Summary

## Scope

Flutter/Dart project — "E2E" here means the project's own established
convention of `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` files: the real DI graph (`sl`),
real `Cubit` -> `Repository` -> `DataSource` -> `ApiClient` -> `Dio`
pipeline (both real interceptors attached), with only the transport
boundary (`HttpClientAdapter`) and native plugins faked (no
device/simulator/CI exists yet per AGENTS.md). Playwright/browser E2E
does not apply to this codebase.

Target feature: **export** (story 7.1 — request a period export & job
status tracking), chosen because capture, entries, and chat already had
this level of coverage; export did not.

## Generated Tests

### E2E Tests

- [x] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — 5 tests, driven
  directly against the real, DI-resolved `ExportJobCubit`:
  - Happy path: `start()` → genuine `export-summary-create` POST (URL,
    headers, periodEnd bumped to local end-of-day before UTC
    conversion) → real `Timer.periodic` poll loop → genuine
    `export-status-get/{jobId}` GETs → Pendente → Processando →
    Concluído (`ExportOutcome.narrativeReady`); also asserts polling
    really stops once terminal.
  - Narrativa falhou: `narrativeStatus: failed` maps to
    `ExportOutcome.narrativeUnavailable` through the real DTO mapping.
  - Período vazio: `errorCode: EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` maps through the
    real `Failure.fromCode` → `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`.
  - Erro: a non-empty-period error code (`AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`) maps
    to the generic `ExportJobState.error`.
  - Review-patch coverage: `export-summary-create` failing with a
    *retryable* code (`RATE_LIMITED`) is never retried — proves
    `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions`' real wiring for this
    function (previously only exercised in isolation or against a fake
    repository, never through the real Dio pipeline).

- [x] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` / `test/features/export/
  export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — closed a test-pinning gap flagged by
  spec-7-2's round-2 code review (`deferred-work.md`): the mocked unit
  test now captures the `options` argument to `getRedirectLocation`'s
  `Dio.get` call and asserts `followRedirects == false` and the
  permissive `validateStatus` boundary (302 true / 400 false); the e2e
  test now asserts `followRedirects` on the request that actually
  reached the fake transport adapter, after passing through the real
  header + retry interceptor chain. Previously, flipping or dropping
  `followRedirects: false` in `ApiClient.getRedirectLocation` would not
  have failed either test.

This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
`export_job_cubit_test.dart` (fake repository, I/O-matrix transitions),
`export_remote_data_source_test.dart` (mocked `ApiClient`, DTO
decoding), `export_status_sheet_test.dart` (widget rendering per
state), and `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s "export entry point"
group (tap → picker → `start()` → sheet, against a fake repository).
None of those drove a real network/poll round trip end to end.

### API Tests

Not applicable separately — the backend contract is exercised through
the same e2e suite above (real `ApiClient`/`Dio`/interceptors against a
faked transport), consistent with how every other feature in this
project is tested (no standalone HTTP-level test layer exists outside
this pattern).

## Target feature: auth (story 1.3 — account creation & login)

Chosen because capture, entries, chat, and export already had this
level of coverage; auth (and vault) were the two gaps this same file's
own "Next Steps" section previously called out.

- [x] `test/features/auth/auth_flow_e2e_test.dart` — 4 tests, driven
  directly against the real, DI-resolved `AuthCubit`:
  - Happy path (signUp mode): `submit()` → genuine `auth-signup` POST,
    carrying the anon key as *both* `apikey` and the `Authorization`
    bearer (this function has `security: []` in the contract — never a
    user token) → session pair lands in the real
    `flutter_secure_storage` channel via the real `AccessTokenProvider`
    → the real `SessionRepository` singleton's `statusStream` flips to
    `authenticated` *before* `AuthCubit` emits its own success state
    (the story 1.6 `markAuthenticated()`-ordering boundary) → typed
    password cleared.
  - Happy path (login mode): same assertions against `auth-login`.
  - Email trimming: a value with stray leading/trailing whitespace
    reaches the real transport already trimmed.
  - Failure path: a non-retryable `AUTH_INVALID` (401) surfaces as
    `formError` with `Failure.message` verbatim, status returns to
    idle, nothing is written to the real secure-storage channel, and
    `SessionRepository.currentStatus` is never touched.

This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
`auth_cubit_test.dart` (fake `AuthRepository`/`SessionRepository`),
`auth_repository_impl_test.dart` / `auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`

through to a real secure-storage write and a real
`SessionRepository.statusStream` flip, in one `submit()` call.

### API Tests

Not applicable separately, same rationale as the export entry above —
exercised through the same e2e suite.

## Target feature: dashboard (story 8.1 — on-demand dashboard aggregation

  - **(story 8.2 addition)** A `DashboardNarrativeCubit — spec-8-2

This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
`dashboard_cubit_test.dart`/`dashboard_narrative_cubit_test.dart`
(hand-written fake `DashboardRepository`/`PendingEntryWriteTracker`,

13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.
16	
17	**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. Render the resulting text below the chart only in the >30-entries state — the only scenario with a narrative in the prototype — with a dedicated "unavailable, tap to retry" message when just that fetch fails; the chart itself never degrades.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).
23	- New `DashboardNarrativeCubit extends Cubit<Resource<String>>`, mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape: `registerLazySingleton`, constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites` (recompute on every entry write, same as the aggregate), `load()` is generation-guarded.
24	- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
25	- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
26	- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
27	- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
28	- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
29	- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce` **only when `DashboardCubit`'s own current state is `ResourceData` with `totalCount > 30`** (i.e. only when the narrative section is actually visible) — never for `0`/`1`/mid-range counts, consistent with Never below. The announced text is the same fixed `"Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora"` copy the narrative section itself renders, never the raw `Failure.message` (keeps VoiceOver and on-screen text in sync; amended, see Spec Change Log).
30	
31	**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.
32	
33	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
34	
35	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
36	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
37	| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
38	| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
39	| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
40	| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.

**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. Render the resulting text below the chart only in the >30-entries state — the only scenario with a narrative in the prototype — with a dedicated "unavailable, tap to retry" message when just that fetch fails; the chart itself never degrades.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).
- New `DashboardNarrativeCubit extends Cubit<Resource<String>>`, mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape: `registerLazySingleton`, constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites` (recompute on every entry write, same as the aggregate), `load()` is generation-guarded.
- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce` **only when `DashboardCubit`'s own current state is `ResourceData` with `totalCount > 30`** (i.e. only when the narrative section is actually visible) — never for `0`/`1`/mid-range counts, consistent with Never below. The announced text is the same fixed `"Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora"` copy the narrative section itself renders, never the raw `Failure.message` (keeps VoiceOver and on-screen text in sync; amended, see Spec Change Log).

**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/dashboard/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart:10-22` -- add `getNarrative({required period})` beside `getAggregate`
- `lib/features/dashboard/data/datasources/dashboard_remote_data_source.dart:12-33` -- add `getNarrative`, same `.get('dashboard-narrative-get', queryParameters:)` + try/catch-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`
- `lib/features/dashboard/data/repositories/dashboard_repository_impl.dart:13-25` -- add thin pass-through `getNarrative`
- new `lib/features/dashboard/data/models/dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- `@JsonSerializable()`, fields `text`/`generatedAt`, `toDomain() => text`; mirror `dashboard_aggregate_dto.dart:1-31`'s structure
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/cubit/dashboard_cubit.dart:25-68` -- template for new `presentation/cubit/dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` (`Cubit<Resource<String>>`, same constructor/`load()`/generation-guard/`confirmedWrites` shape)
- `lib/features/dashboard/dashboard_injection.dart:21-45` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` as a second `registerLazySingleton`, same dependencies as `DashboardCubit`
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_chart_section.dart:131-213` (`_populatedCard`) -- thread `BuildContext` in, add a narrative `BlocBuilder<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>` only inside the `totalCount > 30` branch
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:17-30,45-48,65-76,183-193` -- add `narrativeCubit` constructor param, provide it, call `.load()` in `initState`, add a `BlocListener` announcing its `ResourceError`
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:135-140` -- pass `sl<DashboardNarrativeCubit>()` to `AccountSettingsScreen`
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:780-807` -- append `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20) beside the other dashboard tokens
- `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart:86-139` -- `_FakeDashboardRepository` needs a `getNarrative` override once the interface grows; add a `_buildNarrativeCubit` helper mirroring `_buildDashboardCubit`
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1689-1736` -- `GET /dashboard/narrative` contract (frozen)
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:110,113` + raw `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`/`narrativeFailed` logic -- source of the >30-only scoping and the retry-link behavior

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `dashboard_repository.dart` / `dashboard_remote_data_source.dart` / `dashboard_repository_impl.dart` -- add `getNarrative` -- new backend call, same layering as `getAggregate`
- [x] `dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- full-contract DTO + `toDomain()` -- DTO convention (RNF09)
- [x] `dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` -- `Cubit<Resource<String>>`, `load()` + generation guard + `confirmedWrites` subscription -- mirrors `DashboardCubit`
- [x] `dashboard_injection.dart` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` -- DI wiring
- [x] `dashboard_chart_section.dart` -- render narrative text/error/retry inside the `>30` branch only -- I/O matrix
- [x] `account_settings_screen.dart` + `app_router.dart` -- wire the new cubit through, `load()` on open, announce errors -- screen integration
- [x] `design_tokens.dart` -- `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` -- AGENTS.md token rule
- [x] Tests under `test/features/dashboard/` (datasource/repository/DTO/cubit/widget) covering the I/O matrix + retry tap + `confirmedWrites` recompute
- [x] Update `account_settings_screen_test.dart`'s fake repository + helpers for the widened constructor

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the aggregate shows `totalCount > 30` and the narrative fetch resolves, when the screen renders, then the narrative text appears below the chart.
- Given the aggregate shows `totalCount > 30` and the narrative fetch fails, when the screen renders, then the chart still renders normally and a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message with a working retry shows — never blank, never the 0/1-entry wording.
- Given `totalCount` is `0` or `1`, when the screen renders, then no narrative text, error, or retry ever appears, regardless of the narrative fetch's own result.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] Gated narrative-error VoiceOver announcement can be permanently missed for the whole screen-open when the narrative fetch errors *before* the aggregate fetch resolves to `totalCount > 30` — the amendment's gate is read once, at the narrative cubit's own error transition, and never re-checked once the aggregate later resolves, so the error becomes visible on screen with no announcement ever having fired [account_settings_screen.dart:231-247] — fixed: added a sibling `BlocListener<DashboardCubit, ...>` that re-checks the narrative cubit's current state whenever the aggregate itself crosses into `totalCount > 30`, covering the other resolution order; regression test added proving the announcement still fires when the narrative errors first.

## Spec Change Log

- **Finding (blind-hunter + verification-gap review, confirmed):** the original frozen Boundaries line ("announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement") was unconditional — `narrativeCubit.load()` fires on every screen open regardless of count, so a `0`/`1`/mid-range-count user (for whom `DashboardChartSection` never renders the narrative section at all) could still hear a spoken "narrative failed" announcement for a UI element never shown to them. This also sits in tension with the adjacent frozen `Never: show narrative text or its error for 0/1-count states` line — an audio announcement is a form of showing that error. A second, smaller defect rode along: the announcement used the raw, unsanitized `Failure.message` while the on-screen narrative-unavailable text is fixed copy, so VoiceOver and sighted users received different wording for the same failure.
- **Amendment:** the `_announce` line above now gates on `DashboardCubit`'s own current state (`ResourceData` with `totalCount > 30`) before announcing a narrative error, and announces the same fixed `"Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora"` copy rather than `Failure.message`. This is a read of `DashboardCubit`'s state value from within the narrative listener, not a merge of the two `Resource`s into one state object — the existing `Never: couple the two Resources` line is unaffected.
- **Known-bad state avoided:** a user with 30 or fewer entries hearing a spoken error about a paragraph that was never on screen, and VoiceOver/sighted users hearing/reading two different error messages for the same narrative failure.
- **KEEP:** every other part of the shipped implementation (DTO, repository/datasource methods, `DashboardNarrativeCubit`'s shape, DI wiring, the `>30`-only visual scoping, the retry link's behavior, the >30-only I/O matrix, all passing tests) is correct and must survive re-derivation untouched — only the `AccountSettingsScreen` announcement's gating condition and announced text change. Routed to the human (AskUserQuestion) given the root cause sat inside `<frozen-after-approval>`; resolved in favor of a direct patch over a full revert-and-replan, per explicit human instruction to use technical judgment, consistent with the same precedent set on spec-8-1.

## Design Notes

The >30-only scoping isn't stated verbatim in `epics.md`'s AC text ("Given the chart has rendered with data") but is unambiguous once cross-referenced: `prototype-extract.md:110-113` gives the AI narrative only to "mais de 30 registros," gives "uma entrada" its own non-AI hardcoded line (already shipped verbatim in spec-8-1), and gives "zero entradas" explicitly "no summary paragraph" — and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum itself has only three options, with `narrativeFailed` forcibly set to the `'Mais de 30'` scenario. Firing `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally (rather than gating the call on the aggregate's count) keeps the two fetches genuinely decoupled per Boundaries, at the cost of one harmless extra backend call for 0/1-count users whose result is simply never rendered.
